C queues doswapweapon when needed, dowield, the yumi inventory letter, then dofire, returning ECMD_OK without advancing time; JS throws at its unported dowield queue path.

dothrow.c:dofire() calls autoquiver() when quiver is empty and the option is on, consumes find_launcher() for launcher selection, and consumes doquiver_core() and throw_obj() results on other active branches.
dothrow.c:dofire() directly returns apply.c:use_pole() and use_whip() results on reachable polearm and bullwhip arms; both require implementation in the same task and production doapply wiring.

wield.c:doquiver_core() and dothrow.c:throw_obj() already have JS implementations; verify the reached contracts and source order before reuse.
The later C pet catch/eat at step 73 is beyond this first stop; preserve that target as a later source task rather than treating it as dofire evidence.
